turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_dn_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`, `poscar`
    (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `dn` (the birefringence at
    1064 nm, dimensionless).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST
birefringence at 1064 nm, then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The largest birefringence values in the training set (>0.9) belong to a small number of highly anisotropic, non-cubic crystals that contain polarizable p-block chains or layers (Tl–Te, Cs/Rb–Sb, Cs–Cu–Se). Cubic (or nearly cubic) cells are isotropic and give \(\mathrm{d}n=0\).

Candidate structures were therefore ranked by (i) chemical analogy to those outliers and (ii) lattice anisotropy (max/min cell-edge ratio).  

- c007 (Rb8As8) is the direct structural analogue of the high-\(\mathrm{d}n\) phases Rb8Sb8 and Cs8Sb8 (identical stoichiometry, comparable 1.8 : 1 cell elongation).  
- c064 (Tl8S20) reproduces the Tl-rich chemistry of Tl8Te12 together with an even larger cell anisotropy (ratio 2.5).  
- c089 (Cs8Se12) and c061 (Cs8S12) are alkali polychalcogenides whose packing is compatible with aligned Se/S chains (the motif responsible for the 1.16 value of Cs4Cu4Se16). Se is more polarizable than S, so c089 ranks above c061.  
- c039 (Rb4Ge4I12) exhibits the most extreme cell anisotropy in the pool (ratio 3.75) and contains highly polarizable iodide; chain-like packing of this type routinely produces \(\mathrm{d}n\gtrsim0.4\).

All other pool entries are either cubic, only moderately anisotropic, or belong to families whose training analogues never exceed \(\mathrm{d}n\approx0.3\).

Final: c007, c064, c089, c039, c061
